pr_body:
## Problem and scope

Related #107, BF16 store first; cooperative loads remain separate.

GGUF MMQ materializes FP32 output, then launches `store_plane` to add an optional residual and convert to BF16. This moves the final operation into MMQ or stream-K fixup for all 17 existing MMQ block types, without an architecture gate or CMake option.

## Implementation

Complete tiles write BF16 directly. Split tiles keep FP32 partials; fixup preserves the native summation order, adds the residual after the complete sum and rounds to BF16 once. Other epilogues, FP32 output and MoE retain their implementation. Existing FP32 workspace allocation is retained; BF16 arithmetic is not required.

The initial PR (`bfd1941a`) regressed Q6_K/T16 by 1.59% in the original exploratory screen: all 40 output tiles are split across 82 CTAs, so its mixed FP32/BF16 main kernel never uses its final BF16 writer. Its J16 specialization had 128 registers versus the native FP32 kernel's 122, and a larger instruction footprint; separate profiles localized the extra time to the main kernel, not fixup. Those observations do not establish a particular hardware stall.

For a provably all-split launch, the revised route reuses the native FP32 main kernel for partials and keeps the fused BF16 fixup. The bound `ceil((output_tiles × K_blocks) / CTAs) + blocks_per_iteration - 1 < K_blocks_per_tile` accounts for rounded partition boundaries and guarantees no complete tile is stored by the main kernel. Other geometries retain the direct BF16 main kernel. No separate `store_plane` is reintroduced.

Dense MMQ now rejects nonpositive geometry and continuous work indices at or above `2^30`, matching ggml’s stream-K bound. Tile ceilings/products and efficiency arithmetic cannot overflow before that check. This bounds the continuous work index; existing stride/layout and CUDA grid limits are not expanded.

## Verification

Baseline: master `032eb711`. RTX 3090 24 GB / 82 SMs, driver 616.92, Ubuntu 24.04 Docker on WSL2, CUDA 13.1.115, GCC 13.3, Release/sm86.

- Pure CPU index-bound test: `2^30−1` accepted; exact/over-limit, signed extremes and nonpositive factors rejected, with UBSan and warnings-as-errors. Public FP32 and BF16 Store/Accumulate calls reject oversized shapes with null operands for all 17 types before launching a kernel; the max-int ceiling case is also checked. PASS.
- Exact Store/Accumulate parity against native FP32 MMQ followed by `store_plane`: all 17 types, split/no-fixup, multiple contributors, padded K, output strides/guards and input gathers. Includes the real Q6_K N5120/K17408/T16 shape and K256 boundary cases. PASS. K256 uses the required padded activation preparation; the first new test attempt failed that input precondition before timing and was corrected.
- Existing `ninfer_linear_gguf_test` with its independent FP64 dequantized-weight oracle: PASS on baseline and revised candidate.
- Separate T16 public-call Nsight capture: native FP32 MMQ (122 registers) → BF16 fixup, no separate `store_plane`. Prior mixed/full-tile route coverage is retained. Profiles were outside timing.
- All 18 CUDA MMQ/test translation units compile for sm70/75/80/86/89 with CUDA 12.9.86 and sm120a with CUDA 13.1.115; the new CPU boundary target also compiles through CMake. This is compile-only qualification outside sm86. GPU execution on other architectures, Windows compilation, the full server/model, and inference speed were not checked in this series.

### Paired public Linear Op results

Synthetic packed GGUF weights, unchanged `ninfer_linear_bench`, eager execution, 256 MiB cache flush, 50 warmups and 500 timed iterations per process. Timing series used `1e041229`, before the host-only index validation added in this follow-up; device kernels and valid-input numerical behavior are unchanged. These timings were not rerun for the validation-only revision. Times below are geometric means of process medians; speed gain is control/candidate − 1.

| Type | T | Control µs | BF16 store `1e041229` µs | Speed gain |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| q4_k | 16 | 111.616 | 105.470 | +5.83% |
| q4_k | 128 | 264.686 | 248.051 | +6.71% |
| q4_k | 512 | 946.940 | 907.254 | +4.37% |
| q4_k | 1024 | 1906.423 | 1832.697 | +4.02% |
| q6_k | 16 | 147.584 | 145.344 | +1.54% |
| q6_k | 128 | 287.999 | 280.320 | +2.74% |
| q6_k | 512 | 1056.254 | 1037.310 | +1.83% |
| q6_k | 1024 | 2138.110 | 2094.335 | +2.09% |

Primary Q6_K/T16: **+1.541%**, 95% CI **[+1.388%; +1.694%]**, 16 adjacent A/B pairs in eight fixed alternating ABBA/BAAB blocks. The independent confirmation excludes the two pilot blocks. CI uses balanced-block log ratios (df=7); all eight blocks favor the candidate (two-sided exact sign p=0.0078125). Event medians are quantized; the interval does not cover timer/systematic errors.

Other rows are exploratory secondary screens: two balanced blocks / four pairs each. Q4_K is N17408/K5120; Q6_K is N5120/K17408. A separate four-pair screen measured +3.53% versus the initial PR at Q6_K/T16. These are Op results, not a whole-model 5% claim; other block types have correctness, not timing coverage.

The local runner links the registered test/benchmark OBJECT programs and Ops, excluding unrelated softmax-attention sources; full application/test bundles were not built. Runner size: 168,166,752 → 176,620,288 bytes (+5.03%); index validation and its API tests add 41,368 bytes over `1e041229`.

Reproduce with ordinary bundles on each revision, or link those same OBJECT programs for a focused run:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=86 \
  -DBUILD_TESTING=ON -DNINFER_BUILD_BENCHMARKS=ON -DNINFER_BUILD_APPS=OFF
cmake --build build -j --target ninfer_tests ninfer_benches
build/tests/ninfer_tests ninfer_linear_gguf_test
build/tests/ninfer_tests ninfer_linear_gguf_mmq_store_test
build/tests/ninfer_tests ninfer_linear_gguf_mmq_limits_test
build/bench/ninfer_benches ninfer_linear_bench --qtype q6_k --n 5120 --k 17408 \
  --t 16 --warmup 50 --repeat 500 --flush-mib 256 --execution eager --csv-out q6-t16.csv
```

The new store test exists only on the candidate. Use the table's other T values and Q4_K geometry for secondary points. Benchmark records and extra documentation remain outside this PR's diff.
